about: Physics blocks whose maths is a formula (ND3b): each keeps its id, ports and results, and its maths is the Equation below, with a name that says what happens.

params.description: tidal response: Love number k2 over quality factor Q (Io 0.015, Lainey et al. 2009)

references: Peale, S. J., Cassen, P. and Reynolds, R. T. 1979, Science 203, 892: melting of Io by tidal dissipation. doi:10.1126/science.203.4383.892
Segatz, M., Spohn, T., Ross, M. N. and Schubert, G. 1988, Icarus 75, 187: tidal dissipation in Io https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/1988Icar...75..187S
Lainey, V. et al. 2009, Nature 459, 957 (Io's k2/Q). doi:10.1038/nature08108

equation.name: Heat squeezed out of a world by its stretched orbit
equation.formula:
n = sqrt(G * M / (a * a * a))
r5 = R * R * R * R * R
a6 = a * a * a * a * a * a
P = 21/2 * kq * G * M * M * r5 * n * e * e / a6

kq.name: how strongly the world flexes and loses heat (k2/Q)

source.text: Murray, C. D. and Dermott, S. F. 1999, Solar System Dynamics, Cambridge University Press

explain.curious: A moon on a slightly oval orbit is squeezed and relaxed every lap, and the flexing heats it. It makes Io the most volcanic place known.
explain.science: Heating of a synchronously rotating satellite by its eccentricity tide, for small e. Power scales as the fifth power of the satellite's radius and falls as distance to the power -7.5, so it is sensitive to everything.

params.description: moment of inertia factor I/(m R²); 0.4 for a uniform sphere

references: Gladman, B. et al. 1996, Icarus 122, 166: synchronous locking of tidally evolving satellites, eq. 9 https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/1996Icar..122..166G
atoms.shown: t = ω a⁶ I Q / (3 G M² k2 R⁵), I = α m R²

equation.name: Time for a world to turn one face to its host
equation.formula:
I = cI * m * R * R
a6 = a * a * a * a * a * a
r5 = R * R * R * R * R
t = w * a6 * I * Q / (3 * G * M * M * k2 * r5)

w.name: how fast it spun at first

t.name: time until one face always points inward

source.text: Gladman, B. et al. 1996, Icarus 122, 166, Synchronous locking of tidally evolving satellites

explain.curious: Tides slowly brake a spinning world until one face always points at its partner, as the Moon does. Close in, it takes a few million years; far out, longer than the universe has existed.
explain.science: Despinning time for a body whose tidal response is a constant Q, from an initial spin to synchronous. Order-of-magnitude only: Q and k2 are uncertain by factors of several, and Q depends on frequency.
